recognize_zh: CD3 免疫染色中，棕色膜狀陽性的小 T 淋巴球聚集在兩側淋巴組織並散布於中間，而中央擴張竇內的大型組織球（淡藍、圓形空泡狀核、豐富淡染細胞質）為陰性；這是 Rosai-Dorfman 病竇內組織球的背景 T 細胞分布。
features: Strong membranous CD3 staining of small lymphocytes clustered at the edges and scattered in the field
Large histiocytes with round vesicular nuclei and abundant pale cytoplasm are CD3-negative
Central sinusoidal area populated by CD3-negative large cells
Some CD3-positive lymphocytes appear to lie within histiocyte cytoplasm (possible emperipolesis)
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD3 in a lymph node highlights numerous small T lymphocytes at the periphery of an expanded sinus and scattered within it. The large sinus histiocytes with vesicular nuclei and abundant pale cytoplasm are negative. The T cells are small and cytologically bland, without a population of large atypical CD3-positive cells. Findings support a reactive T-cell background surrounding a CD3-negative histiocytic sinus infiltrate, consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease when combined with S100 positivity and emperipolesis.

ddx.vs: ALCL cells in sinuses are CD30-positive with frequent loss of CD3, and are hallmark cells rather than S100-positive histiocytes with emperipolesis.
LCH cells have grooved nuclei with eosinophils and are CD1a and langerin positive.
Ordinary sinus histiocytes are S100-negative and lack prominent emperipolesis.
